title: Edmund and the Letters
premise: Quentin Nakamura has spent years keeping her heart as carefully archived as her late grandfather's lighthouse logs, writing romance novels under a pen name while insisting love is a story she tells rather than lives. When she hires Edmund Voss, a quiet stranger with a lawyer's careful hands and a secret of his own, to pose as her boyfriend at the Nakamura family reunion, the performance dissolves by dessert into something dangerously mutual. But Edmund's real errand on the island—contesting an inheritance that could strip Quentin's family of the lighthouse itself—forces them both to choose between loyalty and truth. In the end, Edmund abandons his client's claim, Quentin publishes under her own name for the first time, and they keep the light burning together through one last storm.
about_author: Sable Oyelaran is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse keeper's logs along the northern coast before turning to fiction. She writes slow-burn romances about people who mistake silence for safety.

chapters.title: The Last Train Schedule
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She catalogs her quiet life: the lighthouse cottage, her pseudonym, her rule against second acts. A letter arrives announcing the Nakamura family reunion—and her ex-fiancé will attend with his new wife. Emotional beat: dread disguised as organization.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Ferry Dock
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He arrives on the island posing as a tourist, carrying a law firm's file he hasn't fully read. He notices Quentin arguing with the ferry schedule board like it owes her money. Emotional beat: curiosity cracking through professional detachment.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Desperate, she offers Edmund a paid gig: fake boyfriend for one weekend. He hesitates, then agrees too quickly. Neither mentions why he's really on the island. Emotional beat: the thrill of a small, manageable lie.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They invent a meet-cute over tea in the cottage, laughing until it stops feeling invented. Quentin catches herself memorizing his hands. Emotional beat: intimacy arriving ahead of schedule.

chapters.title: The Nakamura Table
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The reunion begins; her grandmother interrogates Edmund gently, her ex-fiancé performs happiness. Edmund plays his role flawlessly—too flawlessly. Emotional beat: the ache of being seen by everyone except the person lying beside you.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Under the table, Quentin's hand finds his—not part of the script. Afterward they walk the cliff path and almost kiss, interrupted by the lighthouse beam sweeping past. Emotional beat: the fake date becoming fatally real.

chapters.title: What the File Says
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV alone. Alone in his rented room, he finally reads the full inheritance claim: his firm represents a developer whose deed traces to a forged signature—by Quentin's grandfather. The lighthouse is the prize. Emotional beat: guilt arriving like weather.

chapters.title: Chapters Nobody Reads
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She confesses she's the anonymous novelist; Edmund listens without judgment and asks to read her manuscript. She gives him the only copy. Emotional beat: trust extended on credit.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Grandmother Hana's POV. Hana recognizes something familiar in Edmund's questions about old deeds and quietly pulls her husband's ledgers from the attic. She knows more than anyone suspects. Emotional beat: protective love sharpening into vigilance.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The developer's surveyors appear on the point; Quentin rages at town hall while Edmund says nothing. That night he nearly tells her the truth and fails. Emotional beat: the lie gaining weight.

chapters.title: Reading Her Heart
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He reads her manuscript all night and finds a villain who is unmistakably himself—a man who takes what isn't his while pretending tenderness. Emotional beat: recognition as reckoning.

chapters.title: The Firm Calls
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. His supervising partner demands he finalize the claim or be removed from the case—and blacklisted. Edmund requests three days. Emotional beat: loyalty to career versus loyalty to a person.

chapters.title: Hana's Test
chapters.summary: Hana's POV. Hana confronts Edmund privately: she found the firm's letterhead in his coat. She doesn't expose him—yet. She asks what he intends to do with the truth. Emotional beat: mercy offered as a deadline.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Before Edmund can speak, Quentin discovers the claim herself via a town records search. She confronts him on the tidal flats; he admits everything except that he was already planning to quit. Emotional beat: betrayal landing where trust had grown.

chapters.title: The Empty Cottage
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Quentin returns his things; the ferry leaves in two days. He drafts his resignation letter and files a motion withdrawing the claim, knowing it ends his career. Emotional beat: choosing truth after the door closes.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Hana reveals Edmund withdrew the claim and sacrificed his livelihood—but also that he'd known for weeks. Quentin must decide whether timing forgives or damns. Emotional beat: anger wrestling with understanding.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the county hearing, the developer's lawyers produce the forged deed; Quentin testifies about her grandfather's logs, proving the original signature. Justice arrives outside any courtroom Edmund built. Emotional beat: the family standing together, with one seat empty.

chapters.title: Last Train Out
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Defeated professionally but clean in conscience, Edmund waits at the dock for the last ferry, leaving the manuscript—annotated with love—on Quentin's doorstep. Emotional beat: goodbye written in someone else's handwriting.

chapters.title: Marginalia
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She reads his notes in the margins: corrections, praise, and one sentence repeated—'I stayed as long as you let me.' She runs for the dock as fog closes in. Emotional beat: hope sprinting against a timetable.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. She reaches the dock as the ferry pulls out; instead of despair, she signals the lighthouse—three flashes, their private code from the reunion weekend. He sees it from the water. Emotional beat: love answering in its own language.

chapters.title: Under Her Own Name
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Months later: the lighthouse saved, her new novel published under 'Quentin Nakamura,' dedicated to 'the man who read every page.' Edmund arrives with his belongings and no return ticket. Emotional beat: visibility chosen at last.

chapters.title: Keeping the Light
chapters.summary: Shared POV, braided. First storm of the season; they keep the lamp together, trading sentences of her next book between checks of the mechanism. The last line mirrors her first chapter's rule, now broken and rewritten. Emotional beat: home as a verb, not a place.
